title: Add selective source includes for git-based sources (reduce clone surface)
description:
## What
Allow dotfiles `source` refs (github:/git:) to specify an allowlist of paths to fetch/copy (instead of cloning/using whole repo).

## Motivation
Inspired by Openboot references include-paths: https://github.com/treadiehq/openboot
Keeps Nexus minimal but improves speed/safety by limiting what we ingest.

## Sketch
- Extend `source` spec: `github:org/repo?rev=...#include=path1,path2` or add structured def in dotfiles config (preferred).
- Resolver copies only included paths into cache/workdir.
- Tests: ensures excluded files never appear; deterministic hash includes include list.
notes: Picked as next P1 after closing Codex/OpenCode conformance audits. Will keep lean TDD: one failing test per behavior.

- Add compatibility fallback/alias strategy if needed (singular+plural bridge).

## Acceptance

- Nexus emits spec-aligned paths by default.
- Regression tests cover path mapping and cleanup behavior.

title: OpenCode plugin parity: compile canonical pack spec to native OpenCode skills + MCP
description:
## What
Implement a simple, direct OpenCode adapter that compiles canonical pack items into OpenCode-native outputs (no transitional indirection).

## Goal
From canonical pack spec:
- skill `humanizer` -> `.opencode/skills/humanizer/SKILL.md`
- mcp `filesystem` -> OpenCode config MCP entry (opencode config), with deterministic merge rules

## Why
Current architecture is over-split (client-file plugin + output plugin + legacy aliases) for this use-case. We want one clear compile path from canonical spec -> client-native artifacts.

## Scope
- Add/adjust OpenCode adapter/emitter for native skill output under `.opencode/skills/*/SKILL.md`
- Add/adjust MCP emission for OpenCode-native MCP config surface
- Keep compatibility mode optional/explicit (if `.mcp.json` bridge is still needed)
- Reduce indirection in OpenCode path handling; keep normalization minimal and obvious
- Update docs/examples to show canonical -> OpenCode-native mapping

## Acceptance
- Enabling `skills=["humanizer"]` and `mcp=["filesystem"]` for `client=opencode` emits native OpenCode artifacts
- Golden tests assert outputs and cleanup ownership behavior
- No regression for Claude/Codex paths
- If compatibility bridge remains, it is opt-in and tested

## Non-goals
- Broad client architecture rewrite in this issue
- New non-OpenCode features

## Notes
Prefer one adapter contract that is easy to reason about:
`compileCanonicalToClientArtifacts(canonicalGraph, client)`
with deterministic file plan + emit.
close_reason: OpenCode native outputs are in place and covered by tests (native skills + opencode MCP config from canonical enable lists).

title: Explore orchestrator integrations (OpenClaw/Gas Town) vs client emitters
description:
## Context
Nexus currently models repo-facing runtime clients (e.g., Claude/Codex/OpenCode) as emit targets. We discussed whether OpenClaw and Gas Town should be added as clients.

Observation: OpenClaw and Gas Town are orchestration layers/wrappers around underlying runtimes, not direct repo config consumers in the same sense as runtime CLIs. Treating them as first-class "clients" may blur boundaries and create API confusion.

## Problem
We need a clear architecture boundary so Nexus can support these ecosystems without overloading the meaning of "clients".

## Proposal to Investigate
Define two distinct extension surfaces:
1) Runtime Client Emitters
- Emit repo artifacts consumed directly by runtime CLIs (e.g., .claude, .codex, .opencode, MCP config).

2) Orchestrator Integrations
- Adapters/plugins that translate Nexus graph into orchestrator-specific conventions/workflows (e.g., OpenClaw skill sync/install hints, Gas Town agent/runtime presets, mailbox/task glue), without pretending they are runtime clients.

## Research Questions
- What artifacts/actions does OpenClaw need from Nexus to be useful (skills, managed sync, metadata, hooks)?
- What artifacts/actions does Gas Town need (agent presets, role files, workflow templates, issue/beads mapping)?
- Which integration points are repo-scoped vs global/user-scoped?
- Should orchestrator integrations run at build/emit time, activation time, or as explicit commands?
- How should state hash and cleanup apply to non-file side effects?

## Deliverable
- 1-page architecture note (or issue comment summary) with recommendation:
  - Keep "clients" for runtime consumers only.
  - Add "integrations" / "orchestrators" plugin surface if justified.
  - Migration/back-compat strategy if any naming changes are needed.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Clear taxonomy documented: runtime client vs orchestrator integration.
- Decision recorded on whether OpenClaw/Gas Town become clients or integration plugins.
- If plugins are chosen, minimal interface draft exists (inputs/outputs/lifecycle/state/cleanup semantics).

## Priority / Timing
Low priority; revisit after core v2 client/plugin work is stable.
